paragraphs: Here's what this song hands you, friend. Israel says "many a time" twice, and it doesn't pretend the hurt was small. Then it says, "but they have not prevailed against me." (Psalm 129:2) Hard years and the final word are two different things.

The turn is the whole point. After the picture of the plowmen, Israel stops talking about the plowmen and says, "The LORD is righteous; He has cut me from the cords of the wicked." (Psalm 129:4) I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you that being stuck is loud, but it isn't the last word. Israel doesn't say the pain didn't happen. It says the LORD is the one who sets people free.

So when you're in a stretch that feels long, do what this psalm does. Say plainly what you've been through, then say what the LORD has done. The ones who hate Zion get a picture of grass on a rooftop (Psalm 129:6), but the song never asks Israel to be the one who makes it happen. Keep your eyes on the LORD, baker, and let Him have the last word.
